plan.topic_summary: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) is a technique that grounds language model outputs in externally retrieved knowledge, reducing hallucination and enabling up-to-date answers. For a 1–5 year view, the key question is whether RAG remains a distinct architectural layer or gets absorbed into longer-context models and agentic tooling, and what that implies for infrastructure spend and vendor positioning.
key_questions: What are the dominant failure modes of RAG systems in production today, and how are teams measuring and mitigating them?
As long-context windows expand, at what point does RAG become redundant for common enterprise use cases, and which use cases still require it?
How is RAG evolving from a static pipeline into a component of agentic systems, and what new evaluation challenges does that introduce?
What is the trajectory of infrastructure cost (vector stores, embedding pipelines, reranking) relative to the value delivered, and are consolidation or commoditization trends emerging?
What security and safety risks are specific to RAG (e.g., poisoned corpora, prompt injection via retrieved content), and how are they being addressed?

sources.title: Corrective Retrieval Augmented Generation
sources.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) inevitably exhibit hallucinations since the accuracy of generated texts cannot be secured solely by the parametric knowledge they encapsulate. Although retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) is a practicable complement to LLMs, it relies heavily on the relevance of retrieved documents, raising concerns about how the model behaves if retrieval goes wrong. To this end, we propose the Corrective Retrieval Augmented Generation (CRAG) to improve the robustness of generation. Specifically, a lightweight retrieval evaluator is designed to assess the overall quality of retrieved documents for a query, returning a confidence degree based on which different knowledge retrieval actions can be triggered. Since retrieval from static and limited corpora can only return sub-optimal documents, large-scale web searches are utilized as an extension for augmenting the retrieval results. Besides, a decompose-then-recompose algorithm is designed for retrieved documents to selectively focus on key information and filter out irrelevant information in them. CRAG is plug-and-play and can be seamlessly coupled with various RAG-based approaches. Experiments on four datasets covering short- and long-form generation tasks show that CRAG can significantly improve the performance of RAG-based approaches.

sources.title: Automated Literature Review Using NLP Techniques and LLM-Based Retrieval-Augmented Generation
sources.abstract: This research presents and compares multiple approaches to automate the generation of literature reviews using several Natural Language Processing (NLP) techniques and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) with a Large Language Model (LLM). The ever-increasing number of research articles provides a huge challenge for manual literature review. It has resulted in an increased demand for automation. Developing a system capable of automatically generating the literature reviews from only the PDF files as input is the primary objective of this research work. The effectiveness of several Natural Language Processing (NLP) strategies, such as the frequency-based method (spaCy), the transformer model (Simple T5), and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) with Large Language Model (GPT-3.5-turbo), is evaluated to meet the primary objective. The SciTLDR dataset is chosen for this research experiment and three distinct techniques are utilized to implement three different systems for auto-generating the literature reviews. The ROUGE scores are used for the evaluation of all three systems. Based on the evaluation, the Large Language Model GPT-3.5-turbo achieved the highest ROUGE-1 score, 0.364. The transformer model comes in second place and spaCy is at the last position. Finally, a graphical user interface is created for the best system based on the large language model.

sources.title: Riddle Me This! Stealthy Membership Inference for Retrieval-Augmented Generation
sources.abstract: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) enables Large Language Models (LLMs) to generate grounded responses by leveraging external knowledge databases without altering model parameters. Although the absence of weight tuning prevents leakage via model parameters, it introduces the risk of inference adversaries exploiting retrieved documents in the model's context. Existing methods for membership inference and data extraction often rely on jailbreaking or carefully crafted unnatural queries, which can be easily detected or thwarted with query rewriting techniques common in RAG systems. In this work, we present Interrogation Attack (IA), a membership inference technique targeting documents in the RAG datastore. By crafting natural-text queries that are answerable only with the target document's presence, our approach demonstrates successful inference with just 30 queries while remaining stealthy; straightforward detectors identify adversarial prompts from existing methods up to ~76x more frequently than those generated by our attack. We observe a 2x improvement in TPR@1%FPR over prior inference attacks across diverse RAG configurations, all while costing less than $0.02 per document inference.

sources.title: Engineering the RAG Stack: A Comprehensive Review of the Architecture and Trust Frameworks for Retrieval-Augmented Generation Systems
sources.abstract: This article provides a comprehensive systematic literature review of academic studies, industrial applications, and real-world deployments from 2018 to 2025, providing a practical guide and detailed overview of modern Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) architectures. RAG offers a modular approach for integrating external knowledge without increasing the capacity of the model as LLM systems expand. Research and engineering practices have been fragmented as a result of the increasing diversity of RAG methodologies, which encompasses a variety of fusion mechanisms, retrieval strategies, and orchestration approaches. We provide quantitative assessment frameworks, analyze the implications for trust and alignment, and systematically consolidate existing RAG techniques into a unified taxonomy. This document is a practical framework for the deployment of resilient, secure, and domain-adaptable RAG systems, synthesizing insights from academic literature, industry reports, and technical implementation guides. It also functions as a technical reference.

sources.title: Benchmarking Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Medicine
sources.venue: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: ACL (Findings of ACL)
sources.abstract: While large language models (LLMs) have achieved state-of-the-art performance on a wide range of medical question answering (QA) tasks, they still face challenges with hallucinations and outdated knowledge.Retrievalaugmented generation (RAG) is a promising solution and has been widely adopted.However, a RAG system can involve multiple flexible components, and there is a lack of best practices regarding the optimal RAG setting for various medical purposes.To systematically evaluate such systems, we propose the Medical Information Retrieval-Augmented Generation Evaluation (MIRAGE), a first-of-its-kind benchmark including 7,663 questions from five medical QA datasets.Using MIRAGE, we conducted large-scale experiments with over 1.8 trillion prompt tokens on 41 combinations of different corpora, retrievers, and backbone LLMs through the MEDRAG toolkit introduced in this work.Overall, MEDRAG improves the accuracy of six different LLMs by up to 18% over chain-of-thought prompting, elevating the performance of GPT-3.5 and Mixtral to GPT-4level.Our results show that the combination of various medical corpora and retrievers achieves the best performance.In addition, we discovered a log-linear scaling property and the "lostin-the-middle" effects in medical RAG.We believe our comprehensive evaluations can serve as practical guidelines for implementing RAG systems for medicine 1 .

sources.title: FAIR-RAG: Faithful Adaptive Iterative Refinement for Retrieval-Augmented Generation
sources.abstract: While Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) mitigates hallucination and knowledge staleness in Large Language Models (LLMs), existing frameworks often falter on complex, multi-hop queries that require synthesizing information from disparate sources. Current advanced RAG methods, employing iterative or adaptive strategies, lack a robust mechanism to systematically identify and fill evidence gaps, often propagating noise or failing to gather a comprehensive context. We introduce FAIR-RAG, a novel agentic framework that transforms the standard RAG pipeline into a dynamic, evidence-driven reasoning process. At its core is an Iterative Refinement Cycle governed by a module we term Structured Evidence Assessment (SEA). The SEA acts as an analytical gating mechanism: it deconstructs the initial query into a checklist of required findings and audits the aggregated evidence to identify confirmed facts and, critically, explicit informational gaps. These gaps provide a precise signal to an Adaptive Query Refinement agent, which generates new, targeted sub-queries to retrieve missing information. This cycle repeats until the evidence is verified as sufficient, ensuring a comprehensive context for a final, strictly faithful generation. We conducted experiments on challenging multi-hop QA benchmarks, including HotpotQA, 2WikiMultiHopQA, and MusiQue. In a unified experimental setup, FAIR-RAG significantly outperforms strong baselines. On HotpotQA, it achieves an F1-score of 0.453 -- an absolute improvement of 8.3 points over the strongest iterative baseline -- establishing a new state-of-the-art for this class of methods on these benchmarks. Our work demonstrates that a structured, evidence-driven refinement process with explicit gap analysis is crucial for unlocking reliable and accurate reasoning in advanced RAG systems for complex, knowledge-intensive tasks.

sources.title: Ragas: Automated Evaluation of Retrieval Augmented Generation
sources.abstract: We introduce Ragas (Retrieval Augmented Generation Assessment), a framework for reference-free evaluation of Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) pipelines. RAG systems are composed of a retrieval and an LLM based generation module, and provide LLMs with knowledge from a reference textual database, which enables them to act as a natural language layer between a user and textual databases, reducing the risk of hallucinations. Evaluating RAG architectures is, however, challenging because there are several dimensions to consider: the ability of the retrieval system to identify relevant and focused context passages, the ability of the LLM to exploit such passages in a faithful way, or the quality of the generation itself. With Ragas, we put forward a suite of metrics which can be used to evaluate these different dimensions \textit{without having to rely on ground truth human annotations}. We posit that such a framework can crucially contribute to faster evaluation cycles of RAG architectures, which is especially important given the fast adoption of LLMs.

sources.title: Investigating Retrieval-Augmented Generation in Quranic Studies: A Study of 13 Open-Source Large Language Models
sources.venue: International Journal of Advanced Computer Science and Applications(IJACSA), 16(2), 2025
sources.abstract: Accurate and contextually faithful responses are critical when applying large language models (LLMs) to sensitive and domain-specific tasks, such as answering queries related to quranic studies. General-purpose LLMs often struggle with hallucinations, where generated responses deviate from authoritative sources, raising concerns about their reliability in religious contexts. This challenge highlights the need for systems that can integrate domain-specific knowledge while maintaining response accuracy, relevance, and faithfulness. In this study, we investigate 13 open-source LLMs categorized into large (e.g., Llama3:70b, Gemma2:27b, QwQ:32b), medium (e.g., Gemma2:9b, Llama3:8b), and small (e.g., Llama3.2:3b, Phi3:3.8b). A Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) is used to make up for the problems that come with using separate models. This research utilizes a descriptive dataset of Quranic surahs including the meanings, historical context, and qualities of the 114 surahs, allowing the model to gather relevant knowledge before responding. The models are evaluated using three key metrics set by human evaluators: context relevance, answer faithfulness, and answer relevance. The findings reveal that large models consistently outperform smaller models in capturing query semantics and producing accurate, contextually grounded responses. The Llama3.2:3b model, even though it is considered small, does very well on faithfulness (4.619) and relevance (4.857), showing the promise of smaller architectures that have been well optimized. This article examines the trade-offs between model size, computational efficiency, and response quality while using LLMs in domain-specific applications.

sources.title: GRAG: Graph Retrieval-Augmented Generation
sources.venue: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: NAACL
sources.abstract: Naive Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) focuses on individual documents during retrieval and, as a result, falls short in handling networked documents which are very popular in many applications such as citation graphs, social media, and knowledge graphs.To overcome this limitation, we introduce Graph Retrieval-Augmented Generation (GRAG), which tackles the fundamental challenges in retrieving textual subgraphs and integrating the joint textual and topological information into Large Language Models (LLMs) to enhance its generation.To enable efficient textual subgraph retrieval, we propose a novel divide-and-conquer strategy that retrieves the optimal subgraph structure in linear time.To achieve graph context-aware generation, incorporate textual graphs into LLMs through two complementary views-the text view and the graph view-enabling LLMs to more effectively comprehend and utilize the graph context.Extensive experiments on graph reasoning benchmarks demonstrate that in scenarios requiring multi-hop reasoning on textual graphs, our GRAG approach significantly outperforms current state-of-the-art RAG methods.Our datasets as well as codes of GRAG are available at https://github.com/HuieL/GRAG.

sources.title: A Collaborative Multi-Agent Approach to Retrieval-Augmented Generation Across Diverse Data
sources.abstract: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) enhances Large Language Models (LLMs) by incorporating external, domain-specific data into the generative process. While LLMs are highly capable, they often rely on static, pre-trained datasets, limiting their ability to integrate dynamic or private data. Traditional RAG systems typically use a single-agent architecture to handle query generation, data retrieval, and response synthesis. However, this approach becomes inefficient when dealing with diverse data sources, such as relational databases, document stores, and graph databases, often leading to performance bottlenecks and reduced accuracy. This paper proposes a multi-agent RAG system to address these limitations. Specialized agents, each optimized for a specific data source, handle query generation for relational, NoSQL, and document-based systems. These agents collaborate within a modular framework, with query execution delegated to an environment designed for compatibility across various database types. This distributed approach enhances query efficiency, reduces token overhead, and improves response accuracy by ensuring that each agent focuses on its specialized task. The proposed system is scalable and adaptable, making it ideal for generative AI workflows that require integration with diverse, dynamic, or private data sources. By leveraging specialized agents and a modular execution environment, the system provides an efficient and robust solution for handling complex, heterogeneous data environments in generative AI applications.

sources.title: LightRAG: Simple and Fast Retrieval-Augmented Generation
sources.venue: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EMNLP (Findings of EMNLP)
sources.abstract: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems enhance large language models (LLMs) by integrating external knowledge sources, enabling more accurate and contextually relevant responses tailored to user needs.However, existing RAG systems have significant limitations, including reliance on flat data representations and inadequate contextual awareness, which can lead to fragmented answers that fail to capture complex interdependencies.To address these challenges, we propose Ligh-tRAG, a novel framework that incorporates graph structures into text indexing and retrieval processes.This innovative approach employs a dual-level retrieval system that enhances comprehensive information retrieval from both lowand high-level knowledge discovery.Additionally, the integration of graph structures with vector representations facilitates efficient retrieval of related entities and their relationships, significantly improving response times while maintaining contextual relevance.This capability is further enhanced by an incremental update algorithm that ensures the timely integration of new data, allowing the system to remain effective and responsive in rapidly changing data environments.Extensive experimental validation demonstrates considerable improvements in retrieval accuracy and efficiency compared to existing approaches.

sources.title: A Survey of Multimodal Retrieval-Augmented Generation
sources.abstract: Multimodal Retrieval-Augmented Generation (MRAG) enhances large language models (LLMs) by integrating multimodal data (text, images, videos) into retrieval and generation processes, overcoming the limitations of text-only Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG). While RAG improves response accuracy by incorporating external textual knowledge, MRAG extends this framework to include multimodal retrieval and generation, leveraging contextual information from diverse data types. This approach reduces hallucinations and enhances question-answering systems by grounding responses in factual, multimodal knowledge. Recent studies show MRAG outperforms traditional RAG, especially in scenarios requiring both visual and textual understanding. This survey reviews MRAG's essential components, datasets, evaluation methods, and limitations, providing insights into its construction and improvement. It also identifies challenges and future research directions, highlighting MRAG's potential to revolutionize multimodal information retrieval and generation. By offering a comprehensive perspective, this work encourages further exploration into this promising paradigm.

sources.title: Benchmarking Large Language Models in Retrieval-Augmented Generation
sources.venue: Proceedings of the AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence
sources.abstract: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) is a promising approach for mitigating the hallucination of large language models (LLMs). However, existing research lacks rigorous evaluation of the impact of retrieval-augmented generation on different large language models, which make it challenging to identify the potential bottlenecks in the capabilities of RAG for different LLMs. In this paper, we systematically investigate the impact of Retrieval-Augmented Generation on large language models. We analyze the performance of different large language models in 4 fundamental abilities required for RAG, including noise robustness, negative rejection, information integration, and counterfactual robustness. To this end, we establish Retrieval-Augmented Generation Benchmark (RGB), a new corpus for RAG evaluation in both English and Chinese. RGB divides the instances within the benchmark into 4 separate testbeds based on the aforementioned fundamental abilities required to resolve the case. Then we evaluate 6 representative LLMs on RGB to diagnose the challenges of current LLMs when applying RAG. Evaluation reveals that while LLMs exhibit a certain degree of noise robustness, they still struggle significantly in terms of negative rejection, information integration, and dealing with false information. The aforementioned assessment outcomes indicate that there is still a considerable journey ahead to effectively apply RAG to LLMs.

sources.title: A Retrieval-Augmented Generation Framework for Academic Literature Navigation in Data Science
sources.abstract: In the rapidly evolving field of data science, efficiently navigating the expansive body of academic literature is crucial for informed decision-making and innovation. This paper presents an enhanced Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) application, an artificial intelligence (AI)-based system designed to assist data scientists in accessing precise and contextually relevant academic resources. The AI-powered application integrates advanced techniques, including the GeneRation Of BIbliographic Data (GROBID) technique for extracting bibliographic information, fine-tuned embedding models, semantic chunking, and an abstract-first retrieval method, to significantly improve the relevance and accuracy of the retrieved information. This implementation of AI specifically addresses the challenge of academic literature navigation. A comprehensive evaluation using the Retrieval-Augmented Generation Assessment System (RAGAS) framework demonstrates substantial improvements in key metrics, particularly Context Relevance, underscoring the system's effectiveness in reducing information overload and enhancing decision-making processes. Our findings highlight the potential of this enhanced Retrieval-Augmented Generation system to transform academic exploration within data science, ultimately advancing the workflow of research and innovation in the field.

sources.title: RAG-HAT: A Hallucination-Aware Tuning Pipeline for LLM in Retrieval-Augmented Generation
sources.venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing (EMNLP)
sources.abstract: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) has emerged as a significant advancement in the field of large language models (LLMs).By integrating up-to-date information not available during their initial training, RAG greatly enhances the practical utility of LLMs in realworld applications.However, even with RAG, LLMs can still produce inaccurate outputs, such as distorting or misinterpreting source content, posing risks in high-trust scenarios.To address these issues, we introduce a novel approach called Hallucination Aware Tuning (HAT).This method involves training hallucination detection models that generate detection labels and provide detailed descriptions of the detected hallucinations.Utilizing these detection results-particularly the hallucination descriptions-GPT-4 Turbo is employed to correct any detected hallucinations.The corrected outputs, free of hallucinations, along with the original versions, are used to create a preference dataset for Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) training.The fine-tuning through DPO leads to LLMs that exhibit a reduced rate of hallucinations and deliver improved answer quality.

sources.title: Retrieval Models Aren't Tool-Savvy: Benchmarking Tool Retrieval for Large Language Models
sources.abstract: Tool learning aims to augment large language models (LLMs) with diverse tools, enabling them to act as agents for solving practical tasks. Due to the limited context length of tool-using LLMs, adopting information retrieval (IR) models to select useful tools from large toolsets is a critical initial step. However, the performance of IR models in tool retrieval tasks remains underexplored and unclear. Most tool-use benchmarks simplify this step by manually pre-annotating a small set of relevant tools for each task, which is far from the real-world scenarios. In this paper, we propose ToolRet, a heterogeneous tool retrieval benchmark comprising 7.6k diverse retrieval tasks, and a corpus of 43k tools, collected from existing datasets. We benchmark six types of models on ToolRet. Surprisingly, even the models with strong performance in conventional IR benchmarks, exhibit poor performance on ToolRet. This low retrieval quality degrades the task pass rate of tool-use LLMs. As a further step, we contribute a large-scale training dataset with over 200k instances, which substantially optimizes the tool retrieval ability of IR models.

sources.title: In-Context Learning for Scalable and Online Hallucination Detection in RAGS
sources.abstract: Ensuring fidelity to source documents is crucial for the responsible use of Large Language Models (LLMs) in Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) systems. We propose a lightweight method for real-time hallucination detection, with potential to be deployed as a model-agnostic microservice to bolster reliability. Using in-context learning, our approach evaluates response factuality at the sentence level without annotated data, promoting transparency and user trust. Compared to other prompt-based and semantic similarity baselines from recent literature, our method improves hallucination detection F1 scores by at least 11%, with consistent performance across different models. This research offers a practical solution for real-time validation of response accuracy in RAG systems, fostering responsible adoption, especially in critical domains where document fidelity is paramount.

sources.title: Retrieval-Guided Fine-Tuning as Noisy Estimation: Risk bounds and Architectural Analysis
sources.abstract: Retrieval-Guided Fine-Tuning (RAG-FT) incorporates retrieved data directly into the training objective, but the statistical consequences of noisy retrieval during training remain theoretically undercharacterized. We study this question by modeling RAG-FT as an estimation problem in a multi-task linear regression framework, using an OLS proxy for single-layer linear self-attention to obtain finite-sample risk bounds. Under homoscedastic retrieval noise, we show that retrieval failure decays exponentially with task separation relative to noise, and derive explicit finite-sample conditions under which RAG-FT achieves lower risk than both target-only and full-corpus training. We then introduce a Distance-Proportional Noise (DPN) model, in which retrieval quality degrades with rank, and compare two estimators under the same retrieval process: the OLS proxy and the literal, uniform-weight forward pass of linear self-attention. We prove that the attention estimator's bias diverges as $Θ(n^{2q})$ even under exact retrieval, while OLS risk remains $Θ(d/n)$ for every noise exponent $q>0$. These results locate the instability not in noisy retrieval itself, but in the fixed, unweighted aggregation of the literal LSA forward pass, which reweighting by reliability empirically removes. We validate the predicted rate separation through direct simulation of the DPN model.

sources.title: CORTEX: Token-Level Hallucination Detection in RAG via Comparative Internal Representations
sources.abstract: In this paper, we propose CORTEX, a token-level hallucination detection method for Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG). In long-form RAG outputs, hallucinations often arise in localized spans rather than throughout an entire response. CORTEX therefore identifies ungrounded content at the token level, enabling fine-grained localization of hallucinations. The key intuition behind CORTEX is that tokens grounded in retrieved documents should be more strongly influenced by those documents than hallucinated tokens. To capture this document-induced effect, CORTEX compares internal representations of a large language model (LLM) under two conditions: with and without the retrieved documents. Instead of relying solely on each token's immediate sensitivity to the retrieved documents, CORTEX also leverages the propagation of document-grounded information through preceding tokens, reducing false positives for tokens whose evidence has already been absorbed into the context. Finally, CORTEX applies post-processing smoothing step that models the tendency of hallucination labels to persist over contiguous spans, reducing local noise and encouraging span-consistent predictions. Experiments on two RAG benchmarks and three LLMs show that CORTEX substantially improves token-level hallucination detection, with each component consistently contributing to performance gains.

sources.title: Cascading Hallucination in Agentic RAG: The CHARM Framework for Detection and Mitigation
sources.abstract: Multi-step agentic retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) pipelines have demonstrated significant capability for complex reasoning tasks, yet remain vulnerable to a class of failure that existing hallucination detection mechanisms systematically miss: cascading hallucination, where errors introduced at early pipeline stages propagate and amplify across successive reasoning steps, producing confident but factually incorrect final outputs. To address this vulnerability, we formalize cascading hallucination as a distinct failure mode in agentic RAG systems, present a four-type taxonomy of cascade patterns, and introduce CHARM (Cascading Hallucination Aware Resolution and Mitigation), an architectural framework for detecting and interrupting error propagation in multi-step reasoning pipelines. CHARM comprises four components - stage-level fact verification, cross-stage consistency tracking, confidence propagation monitoring, and cascade resolution triggering - that operate alongside standard agentic RAG pipelines without requiring architectural replacement. We evaluate CHARM on HotpotQA, MuSiQue, 2WikiMultiHopQA, and a custom adversarial dataset across LangChain agentic pipeline configurations, achieving an 89.4% cascade detection rate with a 5.3% false positive rate and 215 ms +/- 18 ms average latency overhead per stage, achieving an error propagation reduction of 82.1%, compared to 18.5% for output-level detectors. Component ablations confirm that each detection module contributes meaningfully to overall cascade coverage. CHARM integrates with human-in-the-loop oversight frameworks to provide a complete reliability and governance stack for production agentic AI deployment.

sources.title: Entity-Anchored Multi-Document Poisoning Attacks on RAG Systems
sources.venue: International Conference on Electronic Information Technology and Computer Engineering (EITCE)
sources.abstract: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) mitigates factual hallucinations in Large Language Models (LLMs) by grounding outputs in external knowledge bases, while the heavy reliance on external knowledge bases introduces severe data poisoning vulnerabilities. Existing studies demonstrate that malicious passages can hijack retrieved contexts, but they often neglect fundamental vulnerabilities in dense retrieval spaces and suffer from feature dilution and weak generative persistence. To tackle the issue, we propose Entity-Anchored Multi-Document Poisoning (EA-MDP), a highly stealthy adversarial strategy targeting the dense retrieval recall mechanism. By utilizing semantic entropy purification to isolate query core entities and embedding them into five high-confidence context templates, EA-MDP generates high-density adversarial feature clusters. Extensive experiments across multiple open-source and closed-source LLMs demonstrate that EA-MDP significantly improves the attack success rate on three datasets, validating the effectiveness of our method.

sources.title: Agentic Retrieval-Augmented Generation: A Survey on Agentic RAG
sources.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have advanced artificial intelligence by enabling human-like text generation and natural language understanding. However, their reliance on static training data limits their ability to respond to dynamic, real-time queries, resulting in outdated or inaccurate outputs. Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) has emerged as a solution, enhancing LLMs by integrating real-time data retrieval to provide contextually relevant and up-to-date responses. Despite its promise, traditional RAG systems are constrained by static workflows and lack the adaptability required for multi-step reasoning and complex task management. Agentic Retrieval-Augmented Generation (Agentic RAG) transcends these limitations by embedding autonomous AI agents into the RAG pipeline. These agents leverage agentic design patterns reflection, planning, tool use, and multi-agent collaboration to dynamically manage retrieval strategies, iteratively refine contextual understanding, and adapt workflows through operational structures ranging from sequential steps to adaptive collaboration. This integration enables Agentic RAG systems to deliver flexibility, scalability, and context-awareness across diverse applications. This paper presents an analytical survey of Agentic RAG systems. It traces the evolution of RAG paradigms, introduces a principled taxonomy of Agentic RAG architectures based on agent cardinality, control structure, autonomy, and knowledge representation, and provides a comparative analysis of design trade-offs across existing frameworks. The survey examines applications in healthcare, finance, education, and enterprise document processing, and distills practical lessons for system designers and practitioners. Finally, it identifies key open research challenges related to evaluation, coordination, memory management, efficiency, and governance, outlining directions for future research.

sources.title: A Key Factor Extraction-Based Approach for Mitigating Hallucinations in LLMs
Hallucination to truth: a review of fact-checking and factuality evaluation in large language models
sources.abstract: Abstract Large language models (LLMs) are trained on vast and diverse internet corpora that often include inaccurate or misleading content. Consequently, LLMs can generate misinformation, making robust fact-checking essential. This review systematically analyzes how LLM-generated content is evaluated for factual accuracy by exploring key challenges such as hallucinations, dataset limitations, and the reliability of evaluation metrics. The review emphasizes the need for strong fact-checking frameworks that integrate advanced prompting strategies, domain-specific fine-tuning, and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) methods. It proposes five research questions that guide the analysis of the recent literature from 2020 to 2025, focusing on evaluation methods and mitigation techniques. Instruction tuning, multi-agent reasoning, and RAG frameworks for external knowledge access are also reviewed. The key findings demonstrate the limitations of current metrics, the importance of validated external evidence, and the improvement of factual consistency through domain-specific customization. The review underscores the importance of building more accurate, understandable, and context-aware fact-checking. These insights contribute to the advancement of research toward more trustworthy models.

sources.title: Evaluating large language models for accuracy incentivizes hallucinations
sources.abstract: Abstract Large language models sometimes produce confident, plausible falsehoods (‘hallucinations’), limiting their reliability 1,2 . Previous work has offered numerous explanations and effective mitigations such as retrieval and tool use 3 , consistency-based self-verification 4 and reinforcement learning from human feedback 5 . Nonetheless, the problem persists even in state-of-the-art language models 6,7 . Here we show how next-word prediction and accuracy-based evaluations inadvertently reward unwarranted guessing. Initially, next-word pretraining creates statistical pressure towards hallucination even with idealized error-free data: using learning theory 8,9 , we show that facts lacking repeated support in training data (such as one-off details) yield unavoidable errors, whereas recurring regularities (such as grammar) do not. Subsequent training stages aim to correct such errors. However, dominant headline metrics such as accuracy systematically reward guessing over admitting uncertainty. To align incentives, we suggest two additions to the classic approach of adding error penalties to evaluations to control abstention 10,11 . First, we propose ‘open rubric’ evaluations that explicitly state how errors are penalized (if at all), which test whether a model modulates its abstentions to stated stakes while optimizing accuracy. Second, as hallucination-specific benchmarks rarely make leaderboards 12 , we suggest using open-rubric variants of existing evaluations, to reverse their guessing incentives. Reframing hallucination as an incentive problem opens a practical path towards more reliable language models.

findings.claim: Multi-step agentic RAG introduces a failure mode in which an early retrieval or reasoning error propagates and grows across later steps. The authors say existing output-level detectors systematically miss it.
findings.label: verified_fact
findings.rationale: This rests on one arXiv preprint, which is not peer reviewed. The proposed CHARM fix is evaluated by its own authors, partly on a custom adversarial dataset. The reported figures (89.4% detection, 215 ms overhead per stage) also show the mitigation adds latency at every stage. Independent replication is a gap.
findings.supporting_excerpt: cascading hallucination, where errors introduced at early pipeline stages propagate and amplify across successive reasoning steps, producing confident but factually incorrect final outputs.

findings.claim: The external knowledge base is an attack surface. Dense-retrieval RAG can be poisoned with adversarial passages, and newer attacks are designed to be stealthier and more persistent.
findings.label: verified_fact
findings.rationale: This is one conference abstract describing an attack method. It gives no information on real-world prevalence or on how well defenses work. Attack success rates are reported only for the authors' own setups.
findings.supporting_excerpt: the heavy reliance on external knowledge bases introduces severe data poisoning vulnerabilities

findings.claim: Retrieval does not remove hallucination. Models can still distort or misread the retrieved sources, and a Nature paper argues the cause is structural: next-word training and accuracy-based benchmarks reward guessing over admitting uncertainty.
findings.label: ai_interpretation
findings.rationale: src_21c24fb302 states that even with RAG, LLMs can still produce inaccurate outputs, 'posing risks in high-trust scenarios'. src_412149369e (Nature, peer reviewed) says hallucination persists despite mitigations such as retrieval, and traces it to training and evaluation incentives. src_ffc0e99dbc also treats fidelity to source documents in RAG as an open problem. Combining these into 'RAG reduces but does not eliminate the problem' is my synthesis. The Nature result is a theoretical argument about LLMs generally, not a RAG-specific measurement.

findings.claim: Retrievers that perform well on standard IR benchmarks can perform poorly when retrieving tools for LLM agents, and this lowers the end-task pass rate. This weakens the assumption that retrieval is a solved component.
findings.label: verified_fact
findings.rationale: This is a single arXiv preprint, not peer reviewed, and it concerns tool retrieval rather than document RAG. The benchmark (ToolRet) is built from existing datasets. The authors also release a training set that improves results, so the gap may be fixable. Evidence on transfer to document RAG is a gap.
findings.supporting_excerpt: Surprisingly, even the models with strong performance in conventional IR benchmarks, exhibit poor performance on ToolRet.

findings.claim: Several proposed RAG hallucination fixes depend on resources that limit deployment. RAG-HAT uses GPT-4 Turbo to correct outputs and build its training data. CORTEX compares the LLM's internal representations with and without the retrieved documents, which needs white-box model access.
findings.label: ai_interpretation
findings.rationale: The abstracts describe GPT-4 Turbo as the corrector in RAG-HAT and internal-representation comparison in CORTEX. That these create supplier dependence, or exclude closed-API deployments, is my inference from the abstracts and not something the papers claim. CORTEX is an unreviewed preprint tested on only two benchmarks and three LLMs. No cost or latency figures are given for either method.

findings.claim: Reported gains for RAG hallucination detectors are relative improvements on a few benchmarks against selected baselines, which limits what they say about production reliability. They give no absolute false-negative rate under realistic conditions.
findings.label: ai_interpretation
findings.rationale: src_ffc0e99dbc reports F1 improving by 'at least 11%' over baselines, with no absolute level in the abstract. src_2b7b206fd1 evaluates on two benchmarks and three LLMs. src_6c4b033a1c uses a custom dataset. Two of the three are preprints. The abstracts do not report out-of-distribution or domain-shift tests, which is a gap, not evidence of failure.

findings.claim: Theory on retrieval-guided fine-tuning is limited to simplified linear models and simulation, so it does not show how noisy retrieval behaves in real transformer training.
findings.label: ai_interpretation
findings.rationale: The paper models RAG-FT with a multi-task linear regression and an OLS proxy for single-layer linear self-attention. It validates the predicted rates 'through direct simulation of the DPN model'. It is an arXiv preprint, not peer reviewed. It finds that the literal attention estimator's bias diverges even under exact retrieval, but whether this carries over to deep nonlinear models is untested here.
findings.supporting_excerpt: We validate the predicted rate separation through direct simulation of the DPN model.

findings.claim: Evaluation of factuality is itself unreliable, which makes claimed RAG improvements harder to compare. A review points to limits in current metrics, and a Nature paper argues that accuracy-centred benchmarks reward guessing.
findings.label: ai_interpretation
findings.rationale: src_ab9cf668dd (a review) reports 'limitations of current metrics' and dataset limitations. src_412149369e (Nature) argues that headline accuracy metrics inadvertently reward unwarranted guessing. Together they suggest RAG gains measured on such benchmarks may overstate real reliability. Neither paper tests this for RAG specifically, so the link is my inference.
findings.supporting_excerpt: The key findings demonstrate the limitations of current metrics, the importance of validated external evidence

hype_flags: 'Agentic RAG transcends these limitations': the survey (src_060ad2848e) presents flexibility and scalability as benefits. Its abstract gives no evidence on cost, latency, error accumulation or security. Another paper (src_6c4b033a1c) shows cascading errors in multi-step pipelines.
'RAG mitigates hallucination' framing: several papers show hallucinations persist with retrieval, and the Nature paper argues the cause lies in training and evaluation incentives.
'Real-time, model-agnostic microservice' for hallucination detection (src_ffc0e99dbc): the abstract reports relative F1 gains only, with no deployment evidence or absolute error rates.

Large near-perfect-sounding mitigation figures (89.4% cascade detection, 82.1% error-propagation reduction) come from the authors' own preprint and custom adversarial data, with no independent replication.

finding.claim: S2 and S3 present iterative and corrective control loops over retrieval as a straightforward fix. They omit that multi-step agentic loops create their own failure mode: an early retrieval or reasoning error propagates and amplifies across later steps, which output-level detectors reportedly miss. FAIR-RAG's repeat-until-sufficient cycle is exactly this kind of multi-step pipeline, and its abstract reports no check for cascading error.
finding.label: ai_interpretation
finding.rationale: The CHARM abstract formalizes cascading hallucination in multi-step agentic RAG. That the finding is silent on this follows from FAIR-RAG's abstract not mentioning it. CHARM is itself a single 2026 preprint with self-reported detection numbers, so the risk is real but not settled.
finding.supporting_excerpt: cascading hallucination, where errors introduced at early pipeline stages propagate and amplify across successive reasoning steps
finding.guard_note: relabelled ai_interpretation: a challenge is a judgement; its quoted excerpt was checked against the source

finding.claim: S3 says retrieval quality is the weak point and that this cluster of work targets it 'rather than only improving the generator'. The RGB benchmark cited in S6 points to generator-side bottlenecks that better retrieval does not obviously fix. Also, the 'earlier active retrieval line' is supported only by src_34b5ac3bb8, whose record holds only an author list and no abstract, so it cannot support any claim about what that work does.
finding.label: ai_interpretation
finding.rationale: Negative rejection, information integration and false-information handling are generator behaviours, so the retrieval-as-weak-point framing is partial. The Active RAG paper is metadata-only in the evidence, so S3's characterization of it is unverifiable from what is available. Counting it toward a 'visible cluster' overstates the evidence.
finding.supporting_excerpt: they still struggle significantly in terms of negative rejection, information integration, and dealing with false information

finding.claim: S10 says the specialised agents handle query generation for 'relational, NoSQL, document-based, and graph databases'. The abstract lists only relational, NoSQL and document-based systems for the agents' query generation. Graph databases appear only among the data sources in the problem statement. The finding's 'bottleneck' contrast with single-agent RAG is also the authors' motivation, not a result shown in the abstract. Labelling both as verified_fact is too strong.
finding.label: ai_interpretation
finding.rationale: The abstract is truncated, so graph support may be described later, but it is not shown in the available text. No quantitative comparison with single-agent RAG appears in the abstract.
finding.supporting_excerpt: Specialized agents, each optimized for a specific data source, handle query generation for relational, NoSQL, and document-based systems.
finding.guard_note: relabelled ai_interpretation: a challenge is a judgement; its quoted excerpt was checked against the source

finding.claim: S5 and S11 stress faithfulness to authoritative sources in medical and religious RAG without noting that retrieval does not guarantee faithful use of the retrieved text. Models can still distort or misread sources, which matters most in these high-trust verticals. S5's headline 'up to 18%' is also a best-case figure across six LLMs.
finding.label: ai_interpretation
finding.rationale: Without this caveat, the findings read as if grounding secures faithfulness. The Nature paper (src_412149369e) argues the cause is structural, which supports the point. S5 itself reports only accuracy gains.
finding.supporting_excerpt: even with RAG, LLMs can still produce inaccurate outputs, such as distorting or misinterpreting source content, posing risks in high-trust scenarios.
finding.guard_note: relabelled ai_interpretation: a challenge is a judgement; its quoted excerpt was checked against the source

finding.claim: S4 treats the evaluation toolkit as consolidating practice, but the reliability of the metrics is itself contested. A factuality-evaluation review cites limitations of current metrics. A Nature paper argues accuracy-style headline metrics reward guessing. Ragas is reference-free and the abstract gives no validation of it against human judgments. The survey cited in S4 (src_668d84068e) has no abstract, so its claimed role cannot be checked.
finding.label: ai_interpretation
finding.rationale: These two sources address LLM factuality evaluation generally, not RAG metrics specifically, so the link to Ragas and MIRAGE is my inference. Even so, S4 implies that more evaluation tools mean a more reliable picture, and the retrieved evidence suggests caution.
finding.supporting_excerpt: The key findings demonstrate the limitations of current metrics

finding.claim: S2 reports an F1 of 0.453 on HotpotQA, a single-preprint result with no baseline figures in the finding. The retrieved abstract is also truncated mid-sentence at the comparison ('an absol...'). The result reflects the authors' own 'unified experimental setup', and the finding gives no way to judge its size.
finding.label: ai_interpretation
finding.rationale: The improvement claim comes from one arXiv preprint and only the abstract is available, so a bare F1 value says little about effect size. The multi-hop benchmarks used are standard, but nothing here shows independent replication.
finding.supporting_excerpt: In a unified experimental setup, FAIR-RAG significantly outperforms strong baselines.

limitations: Only 12 papers were provided, and two (src_8af8d25daf, src_7c1d5b5cbf) have no abstract, so they could not be used.
All findings rest on abstracts, not full papers. Methodological details, baselines and caveats are not visible.
Many sources are arXiv or unreviewed preprints, so their claims are provisional.

No papers cover cost, latency or infrastructure scaling, vector database limits, chunking, long-context models as an alternative to RAG, or enterprise deployment failures. These are gaps in the retrieved set, not evidence the risks are absent.
The set leans toward hallucination detection, so other RAG risks such as retrieval quality, privacy and data leakage are underrepresented.
Several papers are about LLM hallucination or tool retrieval in general and apply to document RAG only indirectly.
The set contains no company-level or commercial evidence.

Only titles, metadata and abstracts were reviewed, and some abstracts are truncated or missing (src_34b5ac3bb8, src_668d84068e). Problems with experimental detail, baselines and ablations could not be assessed.
Several challenges rely on other preprints (CHARM, EA-MDP, CORTEX) that are themselves single-source, self-reported and unreplicated.
I left S1, S6, S7, S8, S9 and S12 unchallenged. Their claims track the abstracts closely, and the remaining caveats (preprint status, authors' own benchmarks) are minor.
The evidence set is small (28 papers) and not a systematic sample of RAG literature, so absence of contradicting evidence is weak evidence.

sources.title: QUERY-AWARE FLOW DIFFUSION FOR SCHEMA LINKING AND RETRIEVAL-AUGMENTED GENERATION [US20260350028A1]
sources.abstract: Systems, methods, and devices for automatically enhancing retrieval-augmented generation (RAG). According to example embodiments, the system may include: a memory storage storing computer-executable instructions; and at least one processor communicatively coupled to the memory storage, wherein the at least one processor may be configured to execute the instructions to: obtain, from a user, a query in a natural language format; identify a plurality of keywords associated with the query; perform graph-based retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) based on the plurality of keywords to identify a plurality of sub-graphs from a knowledge graph relevant to the query; and generate a response to the query based on the plurality of sub-graphs.

sources.title: SYSTEMS AND METHODS FOR CONFIGURATION, EVALUATION, AND DEPLOYMENT OF RETRIEVAL-AUGMENTED GENERATION APPLICATIONS USING MULTIPLE VECTORIZATION PIPELINES [US20260350045A1]
sources.abstract: A system, method, and computer-program product includes displaying, via a user interface, a plurality of selectable representations corresponding to a plurality of collection objects; receiving, via the user interface, a selection of a selectable representation of the plurality of selectable representations displayed on the user interface; displaying, via the user interface, a collection-specific configuration page for the respective collection object corresponding to the selectable representation and including a vector configuration data structure comprising a plurality of entries corresponding to a plurality of candidate vector configurations for a retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) application; receiving, via the user interface, a selection of a vector configuration status cell within a respective entry; displaying, in association with the respective entry, an expandable menu including a plurality of selectable vector configuration status options; and receiving, while the expandable menu is being displayed, a selection of a champion vector configuration status option.

sources.title: DYNAMIC RETRIEVAL GRANULARITY CONTROL WITH REINFORCEMENT LEARNING FOR HYBRID RETRIEVAL-AUGMENTED GENERATION [US20260350006A1]
sources.abstract: [0000]    Dynamic control of retrieval processing of a hybrid retrieval engine is provided by configuring an artificial intelligence system to dynamically control retrieval granularity of the hybrid retrieval engine of the artificial intelligence system to optimize retrieval processing, where the hybrid retrieval engine is a hybrid retrieval-augmented generation engine. The dynamic control of retrieval granularity includes dynamically determining, using a reinforcement machine learning model, a retrieval depth for a retrieval process of the hybrid retrieval engine based on a query, where the determining of the retrieval depth is based, at least in part, on complexity of the query to the hybrid retrieval engine. Further, the dynamic control of retrieval granularity includes dynamically applying the determined retrieval depth to the retrieval process of the hybrid retrieval engine based on the query to optimize information retrieval processing of the hybrid retrieval engine for the query.

sources.title: CONTEXT-DRIVEN ERROR DIAGNOSIS AND MITIGATION FOR CLOUD SERVICES [US20260349865A1]
sources.abstract: [0000]    Context data is obtained from multiple data sources based on a transaction identifier associated with an error indication corresponding to an error in a cloud-based service. A set of error symptoms associated with the error is created based on the context data. Context output is created based on the context data and the set of error symptoms. A retrieval-augmented generation (100RAG) prompt is created for a machine learning component. The RAG prompt is output to the machine learning component to cause it to produce machine learning output indicative of a mitigation instruction associated with the error.

sources.title: GENERATING QUERY RESPONSES USING MULTI-DOCUMENT RETRIEVAL AUGMENTED GENERATION [US20260350070A1]
sources.abstract: [0000]    The systems and methods describe provide a model structure and system for generating improved responses to natural language queries made to a database, leveraging a Retriever-Augmented Generation (RAG) approach within a larger language model (LLM). The system includes modules for ingestion, query filtering, data object selection and aggregation, and response generation. The model structure establishes domain or context-specific filters and employs an embedding based search for the query, selecting relevant data objects or portions thereof. An aggregate data object composed of selected relevant data objects is created. This aggregate data object contains high-probability domain-specific information pertinent to answering the information request. Leveraging this localized aggregate data object, the information retrieval model, such as LLM, can provide responses having improved contextual, semantic, and intentional relevance.

sources.title: Intelligent Alert Remediation Using Large Language Models (LLMs) and Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) [US20260350148A1]
sources.abstract: [0000]    Systems and methods for providing intelligent alert remediation recommendations include receiving a security alert from an External Attack Surface Management (EASM) platform; extracting metadata and contextual information from the security alert and converting the extracted metadata and contextual information into a vector embedding; performing a similarity search over a knowledge base comprising structured and unstructured data using the vector embedding to retrieve relevant remediation data; and generating, via a Large Language Model (LLM), remediation recommendations based on a context-aware prompt constructed from the retrieved data and the alert information.

sources.title: RETRIEVAL AUGMENTED GENERATION ERROR IDENTIFICATION AND REDUCTION [US20260350422A1]
sources.abstract: [0000]    An embodiment receives a first input topic by a question generating agent. The embodiment generates using the question generating agent a first set of questions based on the first input topic. The embodiment generates using a question-answering agent a first answer to a first question of the first set of question. The embodiment executes a first program instruction to transmit feedback data to the question-answering agent, the feedback data produced by analyzing content of the first answer. The embodiment modifies a portion of the first answer based on the feedback data producing a revised first answer. The embodiment updates a SME database corresponding to the first input topic by incorporating additional data from the revised first answer into the SME database.

sources.title: RETRIEVAL-AUGMENTED GENERATION ARCHITECTURE FOR MODEL SELECTION [CA3271507A1]
sources.abstract: An example operation may include at least one of receiving, from a source device, a natural language input from a chat window of a software application, identifying a task to be performed and a type of data to be used by the task to be performed from the natural language input, selecting an artificial intelligence (AI) model for the task to be performed from among a plurality of different AI models stored within a database based on execution of at least one additional AI model on the task and the type of data, and transferring at least one of an identifier of an executable file or the executable file of the selected AI model to the chat window of the software application.

sources.title: ADAPTIVE MEMORY MANAGEMENT FOR MULTI-AGENT INTERACTION SYSTEMS [US20260350438A1]
sources.abstract: [0000]    Disclosed is a computer-implemented method for automated interaction management includes receiving an input and retrieving information from a memory subsystem based at least in part on the input using a retrieval-augmented generation pipeline. The memory subsystem comprises a first memory component storing interaction data with a relevance attribute that attenuates over time, and a second memory component storing interaction events. The method further includes selecting at least one processing agent from one or more processing agents based at least in part on the retrieved information, generating a system response utilizing the at least one selected processing agent and the retrieved information, and maintaining interaction continuity across multiple interactions independent of session boundaries.

sources.title: KNOWLEDGE-INTEGRATED QUERY ASSISTANCE [US20260352782A1]
sources.abstract: Systems, devices, and methods employ a query assistance logic for knowledge-integrated query assistance. The query assistance logic obtains content associated with a meeting, for example, a virtual meeting, prior to an initiation of the meeting. The query assistance logic hosts the meeting where the content is presented. The query assistance logic receives at least one query associated with the content during the meeting, and retrieves a context for the meeting based on the content and the query. The query assistance logic generates at least one response to the query using an Artificial Intelligence (AI) model based on the context. The query assistance logic generates one or more prompts for the AI model based on the query, and determines the response(s) to the query based on an output of the AI model for the prompt(s). The query assistance logic utilizes, for example, retrieval-augmented generation, to generate the response(s) to the query.

sources.title: PORTABLE OFFLINE ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE VOICE ASSISTANT DEVICE WITH MODULAR DOMAIN KNOWLEDGE PACKS [US20260349704A1]
sources.abstract: A portable voice-assistant device includes a rugged enclosure housing an AI processor that executes speech-to-text, language-model inference, and text-to-speech synthesis entirely on-device without external network connectivity. The device features a removable storage interface for mounting Domain Pack archives at run-time to augment AI responses with domain-specific knowledge, including optional adapter weights for language-model specialization. Hot-swappable battery packs with super-capacitor hold-up power and an MPPT solar charge controller enable sustained field operation. A security microcontroller validates Domain Packs using post-quantum digital signatures and triggers cryptographic key zeroization upon tamper detection. The firmware provides mutually-exclusive Open and Secure configuration modes. An optional multimodal sensor pod enables on-device vision processing with embedding fusion. A method of offline voice-query processing using retrieval-augmented generation from Domain Packs is also disclosed.

sources.title: RETRIEVAL AUGMENTED GENERATION USING QUERY ABSTRACTION FOR GENERATIVE MACHINE LEARNING MODELS [US20260350068A1]
sources.abstract: [0000]    Aspects of the present disclosure relate to techniques for automated content generation using generative machine learning models. Embodiments include generating, using one or more extraction machine learning models based on an input query, one or more outputs indicating topics associated with the input query and entities associated with the input query. Embodiments further include retrieving a set of candidate texts from a corpus of texts based on, for each respective candidate text, a given distance in an embedding space between an embedding representation of the respective candidate text and embedding representations of the topics and a particular distance in the embedding space between an embedding representation of the respective candidate text and embedding representations of the entities. Embodiments further include generating a given output via a generative machine learning model based on the input query and one or more of the candidate texts.

sources.title: NEUROSYMBOLIC BIDIRECTIONAL VECTOR-GRAPH SYNCHRONIZATION SYSTEM [WO2026229702A1]
sources.abstract: A neurosymbolic retrieval-augmented generation system is disclosed. Multimodal input is encoded into embedding vectors stored in a hierarchical vector memory with a short-term layer and a persistent long-term layer, while symbols and relations are stored in a knowledge graph. Bidirectional synchronization links an embedding to a nearest graph node when similarity meets a threshold and updates an embedding by reverse-projecting a graph change when a cosine-difference threshold is exceeded, without retraining a language model. A primary language model generates an answer and confidence; when confidence is below a threshold, a fallback model is invoked using a reduced context produced by sensitive-data removal and summarization under a token limit or a defined fraction of the original context, and outputs are fused by a confidence-weighted policy. An asynchronous explainability trace is serialized into a compact binary structure for audit, and offline operation is supported using a local micro-language model.

sources.title: Automated Threat Analysis and Detection Using Generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) [US20260352674A1]
sources.abstract: Systems and methods for automated threat analysis and detection using generative AI include receiving events from one or more cloud environments associated with one or more tenants of a cloud-based system, wherein the events include logs related to process activities, network interactions, and file modifications; retrieving and updating threat intelligence data from a dynamically updated RAG system with a vector store, wherein the threat intelligence data includes external data and data from internal resources; calculating an anomaly score using the events in combination with updated threat intelligence data retrieved from the RAG system; and generating an alert responsive to the anomaly score exceeding a predefined threshold.

sources.title: SYSTEMS AND METHODS FOR IMPLEMENTING ACCESS CONTROL POLICIES IN CONJUNCTION WITH SEMANTIC SEARCH ENGINES [US20260350205A1]
sources.abstract: Examples provide a system including a memory storing an access control enforcement service, and a processor. The processor is configured to receive a record and access control information associated with the record. The access control information indicates a set of user groups having access to at least a portion of the record. The processor generates at least one vector chunk embedding and stores the at least one vector chunk embedding in a vector database. The vector chunk embedding includes vector data of a segment of the record and a reference to the access control information associated with the record. Responsive to detecting a modification of the access control information associated with the record, the processor updates, in the vector database, the at least one vector chunk embedding associated with the record according to the modification.

sources.title: ACCESS-RESTRICTED INPUT DATA RETRIEVAL FOR RAG ARCHITECTURE [CA3271505A1]
sources.abstract: An example operation may include at least one of receiving a natural language query associated with a profile, determining access privileges of the profile to a database, filtering documents within the database to remove document content that does not match the access privileges, retrieving a subset of the filtered documents based on a comparison of the filtered documents to the natural language query in vector space, generating a response to the natural language query based on the retrieved subset of filtered documents, and sending the response to a software application.

sources.title: LANGUAGE-AGNOSTIC RETRIEVAL AUGMENTED GENERATION FOR CODEBASES [EP4835686A1]
sources.abstract: Methods, apparatuses, and products for language-agnostic retrieval augmented generation for codebases, including: generating a plurality of chunks from a codebase; generating, from the plurality of chunks, a plurality of enhanced chunks, wherein generating the plurality of enhanced chunks comprises: providing, for each chunk of the plurality of chunks, a particular chunk and one or more proximate chunks that are sequentially proximate to the particular chunk as input to a machine learning model that redefines one or more boundaries of the particular chunk based on the one or more proximate chunks; receiving, as output from the machine learning model and in response to the input, a particular enhanced chunk of the plurality of enhanced chunks; and generating a plurality of indexes for the plurality of enhanced chunks each corresponding to a different search strategy of a plurality of search strategies.

sources.title: METHOD FOR INDUSTRIAL PLANT OPERATION [EP4835598A1]
sources.abstract: The invention provides a method computer-implemented method for industrial plant operation, the method comprising obtaining image data comprising a plurality of frames of a plant monitoring and control graphical user interface, GUI, for an industrial plant, inputting the image data into a multi-modal Neural generative model, the multi-modal Neural generative model generating, based on the image data, a first output comprising an analysis of a change of industrial plant operation as derived from the plurality of frames, including a current frame and a previous frame, thereby providing operational context for a present state of the industrial plant, the multi-modal Neural generative model generating, based on the first output and optionally the image data, a second output comprising an analysis of the present state of the industrial plant taking into account the operational context, the multi-modal Neural generative model generating: user support output including: a representation of the analysis result of the analysis of the change and/or present state and/or suggested user actions associated with the plant operation and/or a query response responsive to a user query associated with the plant operation, and/or control output configured to control automated actions associated with the plant operation, wherein generating the user support output and/or the control output employs retrieval augmented generation, RAG, using a knowledge base associated with the plant operation.

sources.title: MANAGING ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE (AI) MODEL OUTPUTS USING RETRIEVAL-AUGMENTED GENERATION (RAG) EXPLAINABILITY REPORTS [US20260339989A1]
sources.abstract: [0000]    Methods and systems for providing computer-implemented services using generative AI models are disclosed. To do so, a prompt may be obtained for a first generative AI model of the generative AI models. A data source analysis process may be performed to obtain a sub-set of the data sources. The prompt, the first generative AI model, and the sub-set of the data sources may be used to perform a retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) process to obtain a plurality of outputs based on the prompt and perturbations of portions of the sub-set of the data sources. At least the plurality of the outputs and the perturbations of the portions of the sub-set of the data sources may be used to perform a RAG explainability process to obtain a RAG explainability report. Computer-implemented services may be provided to a downstream consumer using at least the plurality of the outputs and the RAG explainability report.

sources.title: MANAGING EXPLAINABILITY OF RETRIEVAL-AUGMENTED GENERATION (RAG) PROCESSES USING DATA SOURCE CLUSTERING [US20260339988A1]
sources.abstract: [0000]    Methods and systems for providing computer-implemented services using generative AI models are disclosed. To do so, a prompt may be obtained for a first generative AI model of the generative AI models. A data source filtering process may be performed to obtain a sub-set of the data sources based, at least in part, on consistency of information content between clusters of data sources. The clusters may be assigned based on affiliations of the data sources. The prompt, the first generative AI model, and the sub-set of the data sources may be used to perform a retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) explainability process to obtain a plurality of outputs based on the prompt, perturbations of portions of the sub-set of the data sources, and a RAG explainability report. Computer-implemented services may be provided to a downstream consumer using at least the plurality of the outputs and the RAG explainability report.

sources.title: ADVERSARIAL DOCUMENT GENERATION FOR VULNERABILITY EVALUATION OF RETRIEVAL-AUGMENTED GENERATION SYSTEMS [US20260340150A1]
sources.organization: TAN ZHEN, ZHAO CHENGSHUAI, MORAFFAH RAHA
sources.abstract: [0000]    Methods and systems for generating adversarial content targeting retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems are disclosed. An adversarial document is initialized with functionally distinct token sequences including an adversarial retriever sequence (ARS), an adversarial target sequence (ATS) specifying a target output, and an adversarial generation sequence (AGS). A retrieval-level optimization operation increases a similarity metric between the ARS and pseudo-query embeddings from a source knowledge base while maintaining the AGS constant. A generation-level optimization operation reduces generation loss between the target output and a generative language model response while maintaining the ARS constant. These optimization operations are alternated over multiple iterations to produce a trained adversarial document. This document induces the RAG system to preferentially retrieve the adversarial content and causes the generative language model to produce an output corresponding to the target adversarial output.

sources.title: HYBRID CAG/RAG WORKFLOW [US20260340000A1]
sources.abstract: A hybrid cache-augmented generation (CAG)/retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) workflow for an Artificial Intelligence (AI) is described herein. The workflow includes preloading a CAG context of a large language model (LLM) of the AI based on predefined relevance criteria. In some examples, the predefined relevance criteria may be the queries most frequently received by the AI and the CA G context may be preloaded with information relevant to answering those queries. The workflow further includes receiving a query and first utilizing a CAG technique to attempt to answer the query based the CAG context and LLM. If results of the CAG technique do not meet a success criterion, the workflow then utilizes a RAG technique to retrieve information from external source(s). In some examples, the workflow may determine whether the query is included among the most frequent queries, performing the CAG technique if it is, and the RAG technique if it isn't.

sources.title: RAG GENERATION EVALUATION THROUGH MULTIPLE-CHOICE QUESTION AND ANSWERING SCHEME [US20260340306A1]
sources.abstract: [0000]    One example method is for evaluating the performance of a generator component of a RAG (retrieval augmented generation) system. This method includes receiving a question from a user, defining a triple that includes the question, a context for the question, distractor response options for the question, and correct response options for the question, formulating a prompt as a multiple-choice question with multiple answer choices, providing the prompt to a model, evaluating the answer, from the multiple answer choices, that was selected by the model based on the prompt, and scoring the model by comparing the answer with a reference.

sources.title: RETRIEVAL AUGMENTED GENERATION (RAG) AND IMAGE SEARCH/UNDERSTANDING FOR NETWORK AND EQUIPMENT ASSESSMENT AND IMPROVEMENT [US20260343254A1]
sources.abstract: Aspects of the subject disclosure may include, for example, receiving an input image relating to one or more network elements of a telecommunications network, deriving an embedding based on the input image, resulting in an input image embedding, conducting a search for the input image embedding in a vector database that stores embeddings associated with images relating to telecommunications network elements, determining whether a particular embedding in the vector database corresponds to the input image embedding, and based on a determination that there is a lack of a particular embedding in the vector database that corresponds to the input image embedding, causing a corrective action to be taken with respect to the one or more network elements of the telecommunications network. Other embodiments are disclosed.

sources.title: AI Agents for Supply Chain Code of Conduct Compliance [US20260340650A1]
sources.organization: CUOMO GENNARO ANTHONY, ADIVI SHYAM, SRIDHAR PALGHAT KRISHNAN
sources.abstract: A system for automated supplier Code of Conduct (CoC) compliance assessment is disclosed. The system dynamically discovers, extracts, and analyzes supplier CoC policies using retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) to ensure assessments are based on real-world documents. It employs large language model (LLM)-generated AI agents instantiated in real time, each assigned specific roles and tasks corresponding to compliance disciplines such as labor rights, environmental practices, and anti-corruption. The agents operate in structured squads, executing tasks in defined sequences with self-reflection to refine outputs. Compliance alignment is measured using similarity scoring, and the system triggers automated actions—such as alerts or corrective requests—when policy gaps are detected. A persistent compliance store retains all results for auditability and ongoing governance. The invention enables scalable, real-time, and transparent compliance monitoring with minimal human intervention, improving accuracy, efficiency, and supplier accountability in supply chain operations.

draft.plain_summary: Retrieval-augmented generation lets an AI look up documents before answering, so its answers can rest on real sources. Research and patent filings on it are growing very fast, and some small software companies already build it into products. The main thing that could hold it back is that AI systems still make things up or misread the documents they retrieve, and the knowledge sources can be attacked.
